terms.gloss: get worse, grow more serious (of an illness, a trouble)
evidence: Cic. Att. 10.4.2: alter in diēs ingravēscit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “to grow heavy”: an illness or a trouble becomes heavier. “Day by day” is in diēs.

terms.grammar: vertor, vertī, versus sum, passive of vertō
terms.comment: Not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections in this form; Traupman is the only evidence. Lewis & Short has in dēterius, for the worse (Tac. A. 14.43; Cels. 2.2).

evidence: Tac. A. 2.82: cūncta aucta in dēterius (Lewis & Short s.v. dēterior)

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 112.
